note: Texts too long to write out, each built from parts, and what `parse` makes of each. A part of `text` is a string, or a map: `of` written `repeat` times with `join` between, where in `of` `{i}` is the count from 0, `{j}` the count from 1, and `{s}` as many spaces as the count from 0. `bytes` is the size of the text as UTF-8, to check a builder by. A case has the options of `parse`, and either `error`, the code the text is refused with, or `reads`: the path of a list or a map in the tree, how many items or members it has, and where `last` is given the last of them.

cases.note: Anchors nested in flow, each holding every alias: 3,000 anchors around 3,000 aliases. The measure of what the aliases copy counts its own work, and gives up past its bound, so the text is refused for its aliases.
Anchors by the thousand on one line, each on the scalar at its end.
Block anchors nested by indentation, 600 deep: each anchor holds the rest of the text.
Anchors that each hold an alias to themselves, nested 200 deep.
Ten references to a list of ten, three levels deep: 44,451 bytes once every alias is copied, which is under the default budget of a megabyte.
The same text under a budget of exactly what it comes to.
And under a budget one byte short of it.
A long list copied eight times is more than a megabyte copied, and under ten times the text: the default budget is the larger of the two, so it is read.
Two levels of aliases behind a comment that only the base reading has, under a budget they fit: read, and the last list has its ten.
Two levels of aliases behind the same comment, a member deeper, under a budget they fit: read, and the last list has its ten.
A text of very many small values is held to the work it takes: a limit of a megabyte or less gives a text 100,000 rule passes. 20,000 items in a flow list are read.
30,000 items in a flow list are stopped.
30,000 items in a flow list are stopped, under the specification's reading too.
20,000 empty items of a block list are read.
30,000 empty items of a block list are stopped.
30,000 empty items of a block list are stopped, under the specification's reading too.
8,000 small maps in a block list are read.
12,000 small maps in a block list are stopped.
12,000 small maps in a block list are stopped, under the specification's reading too.
20,000 members of a block map are read.
30,000 members of a block map are stopped.
30,000 members of a block map are stopped, under the specification's reading too.
JSON text that the fast path reads takes none of the grammar's work: 30,000 items are read.
The same text is stopped where the grammar reads it: with the fast path off.
And 20,000 items are read there.
A smaller limit gives the same 100,000 passes: 5,000 small maps are read under a limit of 200,000 bytes, and 17,272 are stopped.
17,272 small maps, under a limit of 200,000 bytes.
A description of 600 kB, most of whose bytes are the words of its descriptions, takes a fraction of those passes, and is read under a limit of a mebibyte.
